confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is access to a tool during the participant's own work: 'We manipulated participants’ access to sources of inspiration: none, access to Google Image Search, or access to Midjourney (an image generation AI tool).' Each person sketched ideas by hand on A4 paper, and tool-arm participants were told 'that they could use the digital tool ... to gather inspiration for their work'. The scored outputs are each participant's own sketches, so the arms do not differ only in whose output gets evaluated. The form's what_was_assigned matches.

confirmed.statement: Per-arm counts of 20 are supported. The paper recruited 60 participants, and 'Each condition had an equal number of participants and was gender-balanced, with 10 women and 10 men per condition'. The NASA-TLX ANOVA reports F(2, 57), which fits 60 people in three groups. The full text reports no exclusion, dropout, or withdrawal of people, so n_randomized = n_analyzed = 20 per arm holds.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Section 3.3, fifth paragraph; full text, pp. 1-18

confirmed.statement: The paper does not describe the randomization mechanism, and the form says so. The '3 random digits' are the participant ID, not the allocation. If 60 people including 30 women had been split 20/20/20 by complete randomization, the chance of exactly 10 women in every arm would be about 5 percent (my hypergeometric calculation: 0.053). The exact balance therefore points to assignment within gender strata. Gender could be known at assignment, because the pre-study questionnaire, which came first, collected 'basic demographic information'. This is consistent with randomized = yes.
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Section 3.3, second paragraph; p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 16, Section 5.4 ('our sample was balanced across conditions'); form open_questions[3]

confirmed.statement: Coverage: I read the whole markdown (main text, references, and Appendix A), viewed PDF pp. 1-6, 11-12, and 16 as page images, and searched the PDF text layer on all 18 pages.

summary: The PDF supports each part of the assignment coding: individuals were randomly assigned after a pre-study questionnaire (p. 6, Section 3.3) to no inspiration support, Google Image Search, or access to the text-to-image generator Midjourney V4 while sketching their own avatar ideas, in a between-participants design with 20 people per arm and no reported attrition (pp. 3-5, 11). The only gap is that the paper does not describe the randomization mechanism, and its exact 10 women and 10 men per arm (about a 5 percent chance under complete randomization) points to an unreported gender-stratified scheme, which the form already records and which leaves criterion 1 intact.
